passage: A team of urban ecologists studied whether green roofs—roofs covered with plants—reduce the amount of rainwater flowing into city drains. They measured runoff from conventional and green roofs during storms of different sizes. The team concluded that green roofs are most effective at reducing runoff during smaller storms and become less effective as storms grow larger.
stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the team's conclusion?
choices: Green roofs cut runoff by 82% in light storms but by only 31% in heavy storms.
Conventional roofs produced 40 liters of runoff per square meter in heavy storms.
In moderate storms, green roofs produced 9 liters of runoff per square meter.
Green roofs produced less runoff than conventional roofs in every size of storm.
steps: The conclusion compares effectiveness across storm sizes: high for small storms, lower for large ones.
The answer must show the reduction shrinking as storms grow.
82% in light storms vs 31% in heavy storms does exactly that.
The other choices give a single value or say green roofs were always better, which doesn't show the trend.
key: Data must match every part of the claim, here the comparison across storm sizes.
